title: Star Cluster Reviewed Player TL1-TL9 Technology Architecture - Stateful Early Resource Tuning
scope: Standard player technology with accepted cruiser capacity and PDS entry floors, plus stateful TL1/TL2 power-resource and endurance tuning; alien and Precursor technology excluded.
principles: Treat Checkpoint 51 as the frozen architecture/runtime-bridge baseline while evaluating stateful resource mechanics in a separate Checkpoint 52 study.
Use Family -> Sub-family -> TL-specific implementation as the governing hierarchy.
Family rules apply to every sub-family unless an explicit later decision creates an exception.
Sub-families remain similar enough to compare and distinct enough to support meaningful choices.
No flavor text, name, or assumed technology silently creates a new mechanic, target class, bonus, or interaction.
Standard components are the best mature technology normally available at that TL.
AUX components are specialized, experimental, theorycrafting, R&D, or constrained additions and should normally provide modest same-TL marginal advantages.
Not every characteristic improves at every TL; improvements follow the purpose and characteristic family of the sub-family.
Hull TL controls bounded cruiser installation density and major refit milestones without changing the player ship into a larger class.
Historical scenario capacity used for screening does not automatically define normal production-hull capacity.
Exact parity is not required; broad compulsory choice or practical irrelevance is the concern.
All three standard PDS sub-families exist at TL1; availability is distinct from effectiveness, and early implementations remain deliberately modest.
Historical Checkpoint 48-50 scenario values remain frozen regression evidence; architecture-derived profiles use separate IDs and files until explicitly promoted.
Finite tactical resources and reusable stored-power systems are evaluated on their intended timescale; a single duel is not required to value campaign endurance components.
Tactical shield recharge is a core ship capability when power and shield condition permit; a power-support Auxiliary may supply or shift Tactical Power but never unlocks the recharge action itself.

notes: Normal player cruisers use one AUX Capacity at TL1 and TL2; TL3 is the first AUX-capacity expansion milestone.
Checkpoint 48 used two AUX Capacity as a TL2 screening context so capacity-2 candidates could be exercised; that diagnostic allowance is not a final production-hull value.
Weapon Bay capacity is one at TL1-TL2, two at TL3-TL5, three at TL6-TL8, and four at TL9.
Capacity increases require the appropriate Hull TL and major refit/drydock integration; they do not change the cruiser-scale lineage.
Exact second-shuttle-berth placement and high-TL capstone mechanics remain deferred.
Checkpoint 51 accepts the Checkpoint 50 capacity curve as the working baseline; this pass does not reopen installation-density tuning.

pds: All PDS sub-families may engage missile flights, boarding craft, and any other close-range terminal threat explicitly approved by the rules.
Standard PDS cannot attack enemy ships.
PDS resolves before the eligible terminal threat resolves.

Sub-families differ through approved characteristics such as accuracy, reaction capacity, Tactical Power, ammunition, reliability, and evasive compensation; target eligibility is not silently changed.
power_support: AUX power systems supplement but do not replace the best standard same-TL reactor.
Finite storage, operation-specific storage, renewable generation, and core-power continuity remain distinct identities.
No AUX power system grants unbounded or free Tactical Power.
shield_support: Shield AUX systems modify one bounded aspect of the installed standard shield system.
Capacity, recharge efficiency, finite restoration, and Shield Protection remain distinct roles.
A same-TL shield AUX must not make the standard shield generator appear incomplete.
armor_support: Armor AUX systems preserve the distinction between a passive expendable outer layer and a powered protection enhancement.
AUX armor does not replace the standard same-TL armor installation.
maneuver_support: Evasive Maneuvering retains the agreed full-turn posture, defensive benefit, own-fire penalty, and increased fuel cost unless a later explicit decision revises them.
Later progress should normally improve efficiency or compensation rather than increase every characteristic at every TL.
sensor_ew_support: Active sensors, ECM, ECCM, and communications relays remain distinct functions within the sensing and information family.
No sensor or EW AUX receives an unapproved weapon, concealment, or direct-damage capability.
Production behavior must use legitimately known, estimated, or observed enemy capabilities; ideal calibration may use complete information only when labeled.
repair_support: TL1-TL3 damage control is performed primarily by human crews using progressively better tools, procedures, access, and materials.
TL4-TL6 may introduce robotic repair and autonomous diagnostics.
TL7-TL9 may introduce nanotechnological, adaptive-material, biological, or other self-healing systems, subject to explicit later mechanics.
No repair AUX creates free supplies or extra repair steps unless explicitly approved.
utility_support: Strategic and utility AUX systems are evaluated in scenarios where their intended role can occur.
A low combat score does not imply irrelevance for a laboratory, mining, cargo, fabrication, hangar, or endurance component.
